from.place: step 3: A finite resolution by acyclic objects computes the right derived functor after applying the functor

title: A finite acyclic resolution computes a right derived functor
statement: Let $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive] between abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $M$ be an object of $\mathcal A$. Suppose there is an exact augmented complex $0\to M\to C^0\to\cdots\to C^n\to0$ such that every $C^i$ is $v$-acyclic (that is, $R^qv(C^i)=0$ for all $q>0$). Then the cohomology of the complex $0\to v(C^0)\to\cdots\to v(C^n)\to0$ is canonically isomorphic to $R^qv(M)$ in every degree $q$.

source.place: Proposition 13.16.8 (Tag 05TA), bounded-below complexes of F-acyclic objects compute RF

proof.text: Extend the finite augmented exact complex by putting $C^i=0$ for $i>n$. It is then a bounded-below resolution $0\to M\to C^0\to C^1\to\cdots$ by $v$-acyclic objects, since the zero objects are $v$-acyclic and the original exactness is unchanged.

source.place: Proposition 13.16.8 (Tag 05TA), setup of a bounded-below acyclic resolution

proof.text: Apply the general acyclicity criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity], clause 2, to this padded resolution. It gives a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal H^q(v(C^\bullet))\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qv(M)$ for every $q\geq0$, induced by a comparison morphism from the acyclic resolution to an injective resolution of $M$. The terms after degree $n$ are zero, so this cohomology is exactly the cohomology of the displayed finite complex $0\to v(C^0)\to\cdots\to v(C^n)\to0$.
